$comment: The source of sf-profile-picker's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/profile-picker (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

label.summary: What a profile is called here («Профиль», «Вид»); the page language's «Profile» when empty.

resettable.summary: Offers «Сбросить к стандартному» at the foot.

message.summary: Why the host refused the last act, shown in the panel.

profiles.summary: The profiles the host offers, [{id, label, shared, builtin, editable}]: builtin is the standard one, never renamed or removed; editable false may be chosen but not changed. The picker never changes its own list.

rights.summary: What this person may create, {create: {personal, shared}}; with neither, no new profile is offered. Reset is the resettable setting.

current.summary: The id of the profile in use.

open.x-summary: Opens the panel; refused (disabled) when disabled, applied when already open

close.x-summary: Closes the panel and gives the focus back to the trigger; refused (closed) when closed

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

skeleton.$comment: The folded trigger with a bar for the profile's name: the first paint before the host sets profiles (§5.4).

accessibility.$comment: The trigger is a button (aria-haspopup menu, aria-expanded); the open panel is a menu named by the label, its rows menuitemradio with aria-checked. F2 and Delete on a row the person may change open its rename and its delete confirmation (keyboard.row); they are actions of the picker, not effects of the menu role.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-profile-picker for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), detail-adds (the new detail holds the old fields), attribute-and-property, host-attribute (no shim), manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), retired (no new name; kept and noted by the component until the date).

x-summary: One way to choose, make, rename, remove and reset a profile: a field-like button naming the profile in use, and a panel where every act happens inline. The profiles and the rights are the host's; the component says what was asked.
x-renamed: events.sf-profile-select → select (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events.sf-profile-create → create (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events.sf-profile-rename → rename (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events.sf-profile-delete → delete (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events.sf-profile-reset → reset (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events: the detail adds the vocabulary's fields (select and delete ids, rename title, create kind) beside the old ones; the old names get the same larger detail (detail-adds)
settings.profiles, rights: the list and the object the host set as properties, declared
x-decisions: version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: the five events take the tag in their DOM names behind dated aliases, profiles and rights are declared, open, close and toggle answer outcomes; a minor while the aliases hold (§4.10).

events: sf-profile-<verb> becomes sf-profile-picker-<verb> (vocabulary §7: the component's tag). The details keep {id}, {label, shared, from}, {id, label} and add the vocabulary's shapes: select {ids}, delete {ids}, rename {title}, create {kind: personal | shared}; the old names get the same detail (detail-adds). The picker asks; the host answers by setting profiles, current or message.

key-effects: the menu role gives Arrow, Home, End, Enter, Space and Escape; Delete and F2 on a row the person may change are mapped in keyboard.row to the picker's own acts delete and rename (§4.6), which no ARIA effect names.

skeleton: the profiles are the host's data and arrive after the first paint, so skeleton.html draws the folded trigger with a bar of the text size for the name (§3, §5.4); presentation.skeleton names it.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus the rights and the reset; probe.json drives choosing, creating, renaming, deleting, resetting and the old names.
css-variables: five public variables read by its own sheet with the role token as fallback (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.2: open finishes only if the picker is still open and in the page once it has drawn; closed or taken out meanwhile it starts nothing (no outside-press listener, placement or layer) and answers refused, cancelled when its scope has ended (§7.7, gate 36).
version 1.1.3: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.1.5: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.
version 1.1.10: the outcomes applied and refused come from core/js/element-manifest.js (core.runtime 1.25.0, duplication audit A-26) instead of a copy of its own; behaviour unchanged.
version 1.1.11 (2026-11-07): a patch (owner R017). The panel insets its rows 8px (space-1/3), as a menu does; a row's leading padding gives back the difference, so the text keeps its axis.

version 1.1.12 (2026-11-07): a patch (owner C05-C07, docs review R029, which replaces R017's 1/3 inset). The panel is a dropping panel with the context menu's geometry, from the shared partial component/context-menu/scss/_panel.scss: rows and their fills stand --sf-space-1/4 from the panel's edge, a row is as tall as a control of the picker's size (--sf-ui-1/2--control-height, --sf-ui-1--control-height) and rounded --sf-radius--ui, its check column stands --sf-space-1/2 inside the highlight on both sides, the message on the same line. The scrollbar shows only when the rows do not fit; while it takes room the panel is marked sf-profile-picker-panel--scrollbar (component/panel-scrollbar.js) and gives up its inline-end padding, the track the inset, a thumb of --sf-space-1/4 and the inset again. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged; probe dropdown-panels-inset.

version 1.1.13 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.14: the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws are asked for their current names (appearance ghost for link, status danger for error; actions block, decisions C13 and C15), so the template uses no dated alias; nothing it draws changes. Its remove button says status danger (C13).

version 1.2.1: the size rule C18 (2026-11-09): the skeleton's name bar is the size step e6 (128 px) instead of 8em; the same at text 16, 16 px wider at text 14 (it was 112). Also: the panel stands over the page: the overlay place (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08), --sf-shadow-overlay on --sf-surface-popup. Nothing else changes.
version 1.3.1 (2026-11-09): the panel declares a popup place; the loading bar is the fill (--sf-surface-container) (C16, the background system, owner 2026-11-08).

version 1.4.0 (2026-11-10, owner decision C32, addendum 2026-11-09): the panel is a panel of the popup widths: core's --sf-popup-panel-width, 20rem, 18rem in compact density, or the trigger when that is wider, fixed. It was as wide as its longest name between the trigger and 24rem (238 / 214 px with the docs' names). A long name ends in an ellipsis, as before; inside the screen less space-1. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

profiles.description: Set as a property: [{id, label, shared, builtin, editable}]. editable false is chosen but not changed; builtin is never renamed or removed.

rights.description: Set as a property: {create: {personal, shared}} -- what this person may make.

forbidden_client_responsibilities: saving the width on a server

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-profile-picker wherever a person chooses between profiles or views of something and may make, rename or remove them: the admin menu's profiles, a record's views.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not let the component change its own list; answer its events by setting profiles and current
Do not build a second profile switcher

accessibility.focus: The trigger is a button with aria-haspopup=menu; the panel's rows are menuitemradio, the current one checked. Arrows, Home and End move between rows, Enter chooses, F2 renames, Delete asks to remove, Escape closes the form and then the panel, returning focus to the trigger.

sf-profile-select.summary: The person chose a profile. It carries the same detail as sf-profile-picker-select.

sf-profile-create.summary: The person asked for a new profile, a copy of the current one. It carries the same detail as sf-profile-picker-create.

sf-profile-rename.summary: The person renamed a profile. It carries the same detail as sf-profile-picker-rename.

sf-profile-delete.summary: The person confirmed removing a profile. It carries the same detail as sf-profile-picker-delete.

sf-profile-reset.summary: The person asked for the current profile back as the standard one. It carries the same detail as sf-profile-picker-reset.
